The two exit codes `1` were found by the independent review of pull request 14 and confirmed on 2026-11-27 in [Review Round 1 (Pull Request 14)](#review-round-1-pull-request-14-2026-11-27): a new project made with `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 init --skip-make-docs`, a new empty npm cache and home folder, and `PATH` with only a link to Node.js (26.13.1 there) and the system folders gave exit 1 for `command -v buildos`, exit 0 for `.os/scripts/buildos version`, `version --json`, and `help`, and exit 1 for `.os/scripts/buildos-intake version` with the output above. They do not change the result: the wrapper's `version` check, exit 0 with `version: 0.1.0`, is the proof that the rollback runs `0.1.0`.

Where each version came from: the npm cache index holds `https://registry.npmjs.org/build-os`, `https://registry.npmjs.org/build-os/-/build-os-0.1.0.tgz` (integrity `sha512-e1rWFwN1…/aPqW/FA==`, the `0.1.0` registry integrity), and `https://registry.npmjs.org/build-os/-/build-os-0.2.0.tgz` (integrity `sha512-h7vG9pEe…6+Gg==`, the `0.2.0` registry integrity), and nothing else for `build-os`; the npx cache has two folders, one with `build-os` `0.1.0` and one with `0.2.0`.

Result: passed on macOS. With only the pin changed back (and the four skills and the router put back), the project wrapper runs the published `0.1.0` through `npx` from the registry, and the upgraded copy returns to the tree of its "Before BuildOS 0.2.0" commit.

What is still open: Linux and Windows. F-P8-09 asks for three systems, so it is not closed, and t16 and A72 stay open. The Command Prompt form of the guide's steps (backslashes, `rmdir /s /q`, `xcopy /e /i /q`, `copy`, `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd`) has never run; the `0.2.0` release notes already list it under "Not tested yet". The smallest way to close it: run the same steps once on Linux (`sh`) and once on Windows (Command Prompt) with Node 24 and a new npm cache, through `npx` only, and record each step's exit code and output as above. No machine here runs Linux or Windows. A repeatable route is a new follow-up, F-P9-16: a rollback step in the smoke (for example a `--rollback-from <version>` input of `scripts/published-smoke.ts` and a `rollback` source of `buildos-smoke.yml`) that runs the guide's upgrade and rollback steps on the three runners in registry mode, with tests; then one hand-started run. Either route needs no secret and changes nothing on the registry.

#### What the Reports Prove and Do Not Prove

The four `proves` claims, on all three systems, each from steps that ran and passed: (1) every process got npm offline, the blocked registry `http://127.0.0.1:9/`, bin links on, and the launch probe, and the npm cache holds only entries for the tarball file with its integrity, whose content has the SHA-256 `baf54ebf…`: no `build-os` came from a registry; (2) the 9 direct runs ran through `npx -y --package=<tarball> -- buildos` from one npx install folder that holds exactly the tarball's 168 regular files with the tarball's bytes, with npm's launchers, and no other `build-os` folder was below the temporary root; (3) the project wrapper printed version `0.2.0` from the project's local install of the tarball, which the wrapper's own lookup chose; (4) step 10 checked the printed fix command text exactly and ran it as printed through the system shell.

The four `does_not_prove` items: that `npx -y build-os@0.2.0` fetches the package from the public registry (step k); that the registry copy has these bytes (h1, step k); the project wrapper's `npx` fallback with no local install (step k); and every executable that a step ran (the probe sees only Node.js processes that keep `NODE_OPTIONS`).

#### Comparison With 0.1.0

Two references, compared step by step with a script that replaces the version (`0.1.0`, `0.2.0`), the 40-character source revision, and the npx folder hash, then lists every line that differs: the `0.1.0` smoke record of [Smoke Tests on Three Systems (t15)](#smoke-tests-on-three-systems-t15) (its reports from [`buildos-smoke` run 45902212190](https://github.com/brucewaynedecoy/build-os/actions/runs/45902212190), registry mode, the run of that record), and the `0.1.0` tarball-mode run [46004060759](https://github.com/brucewaynedecoy/build-os/actions/runs/46004060759) (`source=release-run`, [Fetch Routes With the Artifact-ID Hand-Off](#fetch-routes-with-the-artifact-id-hand-off-pull-request-12)). ### Rollback Proof on Three Systems (F-P9-16, for F-P8-09)

What it is. `toolkits/buildos/scripts/rollback-smoke.ts` runs the guide's upgrade and rollback steps from the public registry, and `.github/workflows/buildos-smoke.yml` runs it on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, and `windows-latest` with Node 24: by hand as the new source `rollback` (no inputs; `release_run`, `release_tag`, and `tarball_sha256` must be empty), and in every pull-request run beside the `registry` and `local-pack` modes. It needs two published versions, `0.1.0` and `0.2.0`, which the guide's commands name. The existing modes, their guards, and `scripts/published-smoke.ts` are unchanged.

What it runs. A project is made in a temporary folder (`git init`, `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 init --skip-make-docs`, a commit) and copied; the copy is the test project. In the copy, each command of the guide, chapter 4 ("From 0.1.0 to 0.2.0" and "Roll back from 0.2.0 to 0.1.0"), runs as the guide writes it: through `sh -c` on Linux and macOS, and on Windows in its Command Prompt form, made with only the changes that the guide names (backslashes, `rmdir /s /q`, `xcopy /e /i /q`, `copy`, `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd`), through `cmd /d /v:off /s /c`. `scripts/rollback-steps.ts` holds the commands. Command Prompt asks before `copy` replaces a file, so the Windows run sets `COPYCMD=/Y`, which answers yes, as a person at the prompt would. Upgrade step 6 (the pin) is an edit of one field. The steps for an app folder and for an npm install (rollback steps 3 and 4) do not apply: the test project has neither, and the run checks that.

What it checks, the assertions of the macOS hand proof ([Rollback From 0.2.0 to 0.1.0 Through npx (F-P8-09)](#rollback-from-020-to-010-through-npx-f-p8-09)):

- No `buildos` program in any `PATH` folder; npm's global prefix and cache are new empty folders; no npm install of `build-os` is made.
- The route guard (added in review round 1 of pull request 15): before any `npx` command, again after the copy before the first wrapper run, and again after the last wrapper run, no `node_modules/build-os` entry of any kind or version in a folder that the wrapper's helper reads (each project folder and each folder above it, then npm's local project folder and each folder above it, with the helper's own `npmLocalPrefix`), no `buildos` program in a `PATH` folder as the helper reads `PATH` (on Windows with its own `splitWindowsPath`), and npm's global prefix empty.
- Upgrade: the commit of step 1 exits 0, or 1 with git's "nothing to commit"; `mkdir ../buildos-upgrade` prints nothing; both clean copies say "Done." and pin their versions; the five compare commands of step 3 print nothing; exactly one line of `.os/manifest.json` changes; the wrapper prints `version: 0.2.0` with the source revision of `npx -y build-os@0.2.0 version --json`, `help` lists `extract`, `fitgap`, `export`, and `capability-matrix`, `export azure-boards adapters` lists `dynamics-365-ce`, and `capability-matrix --help` prints its usage; the five compare commands against `new` print nothing; the commit exits 0.
- Rollback: `.os/manifest.json` pins `0.1.0`; the wrapper prints `version: 0.1.0`, and `version --json` names `0.1.0` with the source revision of `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 version --json`; `help` lists none of the four `0.2.0` domains; `capability-matrix --help` stops with exit `2` (on Windows `0`, F-P9-17) and stderr holds `version: 0.1.0` and `unknown command "capability-matrix"`; `.os/scripts/buildos-intake version` exits `1` (on Windows `0`, F-P9-17) with the legacy notice and `unknown command "version"`; the five compare commands against the backup print nothing; with everything staged, the tree equals the "Before BuildOS 0.2.0" commit.
- The original project is untouched: `git status --porcelain` prints nothing, the pin is `0.1.0`, and the wrapper prints `version: 0.1.0`.
- Where each version came from: every `build-os` entry of the npm cache index is the registry document or the registry tarball of `0.1.0` or `0.2.0`, each tarball with the integrity that `npm view build-os@<version> dist.integrity` gives; the npx cache holds `build-os` `0.1.0` and `0.2.0` and no other.

### Three-System Run (F-P8-09)

Run 1: the pull-request run [46054715769](https://github.com/brucewaynedecoy/build-os/actions/runs/46054715769) of `buildos-smoke` on `ae521de`. Every job passed except `smoke (rollback, windows-latest, Node 24)`. The reports are the artifacts `buildos-smoke-rollback-<os>`.

The two failed steps, compared on the three systems (from the three reports):

| Step | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rollback 5 (also)`: the wrapper with `capability-matrix --help` | exit `2` | exit `2` | exit `0` (expected `2`) |
| `rollback 5 (also)`: `buildos-intake` with `version` | exit `1` | exit `1` | exit `0` (expected `1`) |

On all three systems stdout is empty and stderr is the same text. For the first step: `version: 0.1.0`, source revision `20f941a…`, and `ERROR [usage_error]: unknown command "capability-matrix"`. For the second: the legacy notice and `buildos-intake: error: unknown command "version"`. So on Windows the pinned `0.1.0` ran and stopped with its error, and only the exit code that reached Command Prompt is `0`. Every other Windows step passed, also the pin checks: `version` prints `version: 0.1.0` with the `0.1.0` source revision, `version --json` names `0.1.0` with that revision, and `help` lists none of the four `0.2.0` domains. The rollback itself works on Windows: the wrapper runs the pinned `0.1.0`.

The cause, as far as the evidence goes:

- Not the guide's Windows steps: every Command Prompt form of the guide ran with the expected result, and the failing commands are the wrapper checks.
- Not a difference of `0.1.0`: the project wrappers are the files of `buildos init`, and `system/.os/scripts/` is the same in `v0.1.0` and `v0.2.0` (`git diff v0.1.0 v0.2.0 -- system/.os/scripts/` is empty); `pinned-version.cjs` in the two registry tarballs is the same file, and the CLI of both sets its exit code the same way.
- Not the smoke's own expectation on POSIX: Linux and macOS give `2` and `1`, as the guide says.
- A product defect of the Windows wrapper on its `npx` route (F-P9-17, new): with no npm install of the pinned version, `buildos.cmd` starts `node pinned-version.cjs`, which starts npm's `npx.cmd` through `cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c`, and npm starts the `build-os` bin. In run 1, that route gave exit `0` for a program that stopped with `2` or `1`. The wrapper's own exit codes reach Command Prompt (the registry smoke's `exit 127` case passes). (Corrected in review round 1 of pull request 15: the wrapper tests on Windows that return `7` and `5` do not run this route; see [F-P9-17 After Run 2](#f-p9-17-after-run-2-windows-exit-codes).) The smoke's direct `npx` steps start `npx-cli.js` with `node`, not `npx.cmd`. So the layer that loses the code is not found yet: npm's real `npx.cmd`, or npm with the wrapper's `npx` arguments (`--prefix <project> --workspaces=false`) on Windows. The wrapper and `pinned-version.cjs` are the same in `0.2.0`, so a `0.2.0` project on Windows is likely affected too; run 1 has no `0.2.0` failure through the wrapper to show it.

What an adopter on Windows sees after the rollback, with no npm install of `0.1.0` (the `npx` route): a failing command through `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd` or a legacy `.cmd` script prints its error, as on the other systems, but Command Prompt gets exit code `0` (`%ERRORLEVEL%` is `0`). A script or an agent that checks only the exit code takes the failure for a success. The rollback itself is not affected: the wrapper runs the pinned `0.1.0`.

What changed in this round (`scripts/rollback-smoke.ts`, `test/rollback-smoke.test.ts`; nothing published, no guide or product file):

- On Windows, the two steps assert the true behavior, exit `0`, with a comment that names F-P9-17; Linux and macOS still assert `2` and `1`. The first step now checks more than before on all three systems: stderr holds `version: 0.1.0` and `ERROR [usage_error]: unknown command "capability-matrix"`. The second keeps its check of the legacy notice and `unknown command "version"`. The pin checks are unchanged on all three systems.
- Four new steps named "F-P9-17 evidence" find the layer. With the `0.2.0` pin (upgrade 7): the wrapper with `no-such-command`. After the rollback: `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help` three ways: `npx-cli.js` started by `node`; `npx` in the shell (Command Prompt on Windows, so npm's `npx.cmd`); and `npx` in the shell with the wrapper's own `npx` arguments. Linux and macOS check exit `2`; Windows records the exit code with no check, because the cause is not known yet. Each step checks the stderr text of the usage error on all three systems.
- The report cleans step names too (`{PROJECT}`), because one evidence step names the project folder.

### F-P9-17 After Run 2 (Windows Exit Codes)

The four "F-P9-17 evidence" steps of run 2, field `exit` in each report:

| Step | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `upgrade 7 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: the wrapper with `no-such-command`, `0.2.0` pin | `2` | `2` | `0` |
| `rollback 5 (also)`: the wrapper with `capability-matrix --help`, `0.1.0` pin | `2` | `2` | `0` |
| `rollback 5 (also)`: `buildos-intake` with `version`, `0.1.0` pin | `1` | `1` | `0` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help`, `npx-cli.js` started by `node` | `2` | `2` | `2` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help` in the shell (Command Prompt on Windows, so npm's `npx.cmd`) | `2` | `2` | `2` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y --prefix "{PROJECT}" --workspaces=false build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help` in the shell (the wrapper's own `npx` arguments) | `2` | `2` | `2` |

On all three systems stderr holds the version and the usage error, for example `version: 0.2.0` and `ERROR [usage_error]: unknown command "no-such-command"` for the first step.

What this shows:

- `0.2.0` is affected too, proven: with the `0.2.0` pin, `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd no-such-command` printed the `0.2.0` usage error and returned `0` on Windows (`2` on Linux and macOS).
- The route of that step is `npx`, not a local install: the test project has no `node_modules` folder, npm's global prefix is empty, no `buildos` is on `PATH`, and the `0.2.0` error text says `Run npx -y build-os@0.2.0 help`. So the wrapper started `0.2.0` through `npx`.
- npm passes the exit code on Windows: `npx` returns `2` in all three forms, also npm's real `npx.cmd` in Command Prompt, also with the wrapper's `--prefix <project> --workspaces=false`. The smoke starts the two shell forms the same way as the wrapper's helper starts `npx.cmd`: `cmd /d /v:off /s /c` with the line passed as given. So the code is lost in the project wrapper layer: `system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd` and its helper `pinned-version.cjs` (the `--cmd` route), not in npm. (Narrowed by run 3: the helper started directly by `node.exe` passes the code too, and the code is lost on the wrapper invocation path, a `.cmd` wrapper started through `cmd.exe`; see [F-P9-17 After Run 3](#f-p9-17-after-run-3-cause-narrowed).)

Routes proven affected, on Windows: `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd` on its `npx` route (no npm install of the pinned version in the project, no `buildos.cmd` npm shim on `PATH`), with the `0.1.0` pin and with the `0.2.0` pin; and the legacy script `.os\scripts\buildos-intake.cmd` on the same route (it calls `buildos.cmd`). Not tested, so not proven either way: the wrapper's local-install route (`node_modules/build-os` at the pinned version), its global-install route (a `buildos.cmd` npm shim on `PATH` at the pinned version), and the legacy scripts `buildos-design.cmd` and `buildos-discovery.cmd` (they call `buildos.cmd` the same way as `buildos-intake.cmd`, so they are likely affected on the `npx` route). Not affected: Linux and macOS (the `sh` wrapper), and `npx -y build-os@<version>` typed by the adopter.

Hypothesis for the mechanism, not proven (no Windows machine here; nothing was run on Windows to test it). The chain on the `npx` route is: Command Prompt runs `buildos.cmd`; it runs `node pinned-version.cjs --cmd …` and ends with `exit /b`, which passes on the exit code of `node`; `pinned-version.cjs` finds `npx.cmd` on `PATH` and its `start()` starts `cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c "<npx.cmd path> <arguments>"` (the path with each special character escaped by `^`, each argument quoted and escaped twice, `windowsVerbatimArguments`), with the wrapper's environment (`BUILDOS_REQUIRE_VERSION`, `npm_config_bin_links=true` and its override variable, and `BUILDOS_WRAPPER_ACTIVE` and `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` from `buildos.cmd`); then `process.exit(result.status)`. Corrected in review round 1 of pull request 15: the wrapper tests on Windows do not run this chain. In `toolkits/buildos/test/wrappers.test.ts`, the test that returns `7` uses a global install, so the helper starts the package's bin file with `node` and no `npx.cmd` runs; the test that returns `5` puts a `node.cmd` stub on `PATH`, and because `system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd` (line 21) starts `node` without `call`, Command Prompt runs that `.cmd` stub in place of the rest of the wrapper, so the wrapper's last line, `exit /b`, never runs. So no test shows that the batch wrapper's own exit path passes a code on. Two causes stay open: (a) the nested `cmd.exe` that `pinned-version.cjs` starts for npm's `npx.cmd` (npm's real `npx.cmd` is a longer batch file than the tests' one-line stub: `SETLOCAL`, an `IF` block, a `FOR /F` line with `CALL`, then `"%NODE_EXE%" "%NPX_CLI_JS%" %*`), which may give `0` to `spawnSync`, so that the helper exits `0`; (b) the batch wrapper's own exit path, `exit /b` after `node` in `buildos.cmd`, which may give `0` to Command Prompt although `node` exited with another code. This is a defect against a written promise: the shipped instructions `system/.os/scripts/AGENTS.md` say that on Windows `pinned-version.cjs` "starts the chosen program with the same console and returns its exit code", and of the legacy wrappers, "Stdout and the exit code are those of the real command." The rollback smoke now has the smallest diagnostic for it on Windows, record-only like the other evidence steps: for the same failing command (`capability-matrix --help` after the rollback), it starts the project's own helper directly with `node.exe` (`node.exe <project>\.os\scripts\pinned-version.cjs --cmd <project>\.os\scripts\buildos.cmd <project>\.os\scripts\..\manifest.json capability-matrix --help`, no batch file, with the two variables that `buildos.cmd` sets), and records its exit code next to that of `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd capability-matrix --help`. If the direct form gives `2` and the `.cmd` gives `0`, cause (b) is shown; if both give `0`, cause (a). On Linux and macOS the matching step starts the helper's `--npx` route directly and asserts exit `2`. Run 3 gives the first reading. The product defect is not fixed in this pull request. (Run 3 reading: consistent with cause (b), not isolated. Corrected in review round 2 of pull request 15: this pattern does not show cause (b), because the helper is started directly by `node.exe` and the wrapper through `cmd.exe`, so the two do not run under the same shell; see [F-P9-17 After Run 3](#f-p9-17-after-run-3-cause-narrowed).)

The adopter effect on Windows: a failing command through `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd` or a legacy `.cmd` script on the `npx` route prints its error text, as on the other systems, but `%ERRORLEVEL%` is `0`. A script or an agent that checks only the exit code sees success. Likely every BuildOS command that fails is affected on that route, not only usage errors, because the cause is not in BuildOS, which returns `2` through `npx` directly; run 2 shows usage errors only. Commands that succeed are not affected. Rollback by pin is not affected.

Severity recommendation (the agent's, for the owner): high for adopters on Windows who drive BuildOS from scripts or agents, because a failure reads as a success and BuildOS is built for agent use; no data is lost or changed by the defect itself, the error text is printed, and Linux and macOS are not affected. So: fix in the next release, with a Windows wrapper test that uses npm's real `npx.cmd`.

The smallest fix route after run 2, a candidate until the cause was proven on Windows: a change in `system/.os/scripts/pinned-version.cjs` only (and its tests), so that on Windows the `--cmd` route keeps the exit code of `npx`, for example by starting npm's `npx-cli.js` with the same `node` (the form that returned `2` in run 2) instead of `npx.cmd`, or by a fix in `start()` once the checks above show the cause. Corrected after run 3: that candidate is withdrawn. Run 3 shows that `pinned-version.cjs`, started directly, returns `2` for the same failing command, so the helper started directly passes the code; the code is lost on the wrapper invocation path, and the batch wrapper `buildos.cmd` is the leading hypothesis for the place of the fix, not shown ([F-P9-17 After Run 3](#f-p9-17-after-run-3-cause-narrowed)). The wrapper files of a project are written by `buildos init`, so an adopter gets the fix only by a new release and a refresh of `.os/scripts/`. The release for it is the owner's choice (see the question below). Nothing in this pull request changes product code or a wrapper. The guide changes in two places only: the `copy` sentence (review round 1 of pull request 15) and the Windows exit-code exception (review round 2 of pull request 15).

| `rollback 5 (also)`: `.os\scripts\buildos-intake.cmd version`, `0.1.0` pin | `0` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help`, `npx-cli.js` started by `node` | `2` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help` in Command Prompt (npm's `npx.cmd`) | `2` |
| `rollback 5 (F-P9-17 evidence)`: `npx -y --prefix "{PROJECT}" --workspaces=false build-os@0.1.0 capability-matrix --help` in Command Prompt (the wrapper's own `npx` arguments) | `2` |

The direct helper step printed the `0.1.0` usage error in stderr (`version: 0.1.0`, source revision `20f941a…`, `ERROR [usage_error]: unknown command "capability-matrix"`), as its check asks. On Linux and macOS the matching step (the helper's `--npx` route, started directly) and every wrapper step return `2` (and `1` for `buildos-intake`), as in run 2.

The record-only step "which layer loses the exit code" names it, word for word: "node.exe pinned-version.cjs --cmd ... capability-matrix --help: exit 2", ".os\scripts\buildos.cmd capability-matrix --help: exit 0", "cause (b) shown: the helper started directly returns 2, and buildos.cmd returns 0, so the code is lost in the batch wrapper's own exit path". That reading claimed more than the run measured (review round 2 of pull request 15, finding 1). The step now prints "cause (b) consistent, not isolated" for this pattern, with the reason in plain words.

What this shows, on the `npx` route on a hosted Windows runner (no npm install of `build-os`, no `buildos` on `PATH`, the launch probe passed):

- npm passes the exit code: all three direct `npx` forms return `2`, also npm's real `npx.cmd` in Command Prompt and the wrapper's own `npx` arguments.
- `pinned-version.cjs` passes the exit code: started directly by `node.exe` with the same `--cmd` arguments that `buildos.cmd` gives it, it returns `2`. So cause (a), the nested `cmd.exe` for npm's `npx.cmd` inside the helper, is ruled out for this command.
- The code is lost on the wrapper invocation path: for the same command, `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd`, a `.cmd` wrapper started through `cmd.exe` (`cmd /d /v:off /s /c`), returns `0`. The same holds for `no-such-command` with the `0.2.0` pin. This is consistent with cause (b), the batch wrapper's own exit path, but does not isolate it: `spawnSync().status` reads `node.exe` itself for the helper and the outer `cmd.exe` for the wrapper, so the helper and the wrapper were not measured under the same shell. The outer `cmd.exe` did pass `2` for npm's `npx.cmd`.
- The legacy `buildos-intake.cmd` returns `0` too. It starts `buildos.cmd` without `call`, so `buildos.cmd` ends it, and its result is that of `buildos.cmd`.

What is still not proven:

- That the batch file's own exit path loses the code, and how. Leading hypothesis, not shown: lines 21 and 22 of `system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd`, where `node "%~dp0pinned-version.cjs" --cmd …` runs without `call` and is followed by a bare `exit /b`. No step looks inside the batch file, and nothing was run on Windows to test a change. The missing measurement is the first task of the F-P9-17 fix: run both forms under the same `cmd.exe` (the helper as `node.exe .os\scripts\pinned-version.cjs --cmd …`, and `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd`, for the same failing command) and read `%ERRORLEVEL%` right after each. The fix is likely a one-line change in that area, with a Windows wrapper test that uses npm's real `npx.cmd` and the real `node.exe`; which line and which form is for the fix to prove.
- The other legacy `.cmd` wrappers: `buildos-design.cmd` and `buildos-discovery.cmd` start `buildos.cmd` the same way as `buildos-intake.cmd`, so they are likely affected, but no run tested them.
- The wrapper's local-install route (`node_modules/build-os` at the pinned version) and its global-install route (a `buildos.cmd` npm shim on `PATH` at the pinned version): not tested on Windows. They end in the same `exit /b` of `buildos.cmd`, so they may be affected too.
- Commands other than usage errors: run 3 tests usage errors only (exit `2` from BuildOS, `1` from the legacy script). Other failing exit codes are not tested.

The adopter effect and the severity recommendation of [F-P9-17 After Run 2](#f-p9-17-after-run-2-windows-exit-codes) are unchanged. The written promise of `system/.os/scripts/AGENTS.md` ("returns its exit code"; "Stdout and the exit code are those of the real command") holds for `pinned-version.cjs` started directly on this route and fails on the wrapper invocation path. The product defect is not fixed in this pull request, and no product, wrapper, or release notes file changes. The guide changes in two places only: the `copy` sentence (review round 1 of pull request 15) and the Windows exit-code exception (review round 2 of pull request 15).

### Owner Question for F-P9-17

> On Windows, a failing BuildOS command run through the project wrapper `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd` (or the legacy script `.os\scripts\buildos-intake.cmd`) on its `npx` route returns exit code `0`; the error text is printed. The legacy scripts `buildos-design.cmd` and `buildos-discovery.cmd` are not tested. `0.1.0` and `0.2.0` are both affected (runs 46056570552 and 46060191323). Run 3 (46060191323) shows that npm and the helper `pinned-version.cjs`, started directly, pass the code, and that it is lost on the wrapper invocation path (`buildos.cmd` started through `cmd.exe`); the batch file's own exit path is the leading hypothesis, not shown. Do you want the fix in a `0.2.1` patch release, or in `0.3.0`?

- Option 1, a `0.2.1` patch: only the Windows batch wrapper `system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd` (likely one line, a hypothesis until a Windows test proves it) and its tests change; adopters on Windows get correct exit codes sooner, after a refresh of `.os/scripts/`; it is one more release through the full release process.
- Option 2, in `0.3.0`: no extra release; Windows adopters keep the wrong exit code until `0.3.0`.
- Orchestrator's recommendation: open (for the orchestrator to fill in).
- Owner decision (2026-11-27): Option 1, in the owner's words: "Option 1; a small `0.2.1` release soon." The release that carries the fix is `0.2.1`. This question is closed ([0.2.1 Release Preparation](#021-release-preparation-2026-11-27)).

Pull request 16 (2026-11-27): the mechanism is shown on Windows and the fix is in the repository, a two-line change in `system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd` ([F-P9-17 Mechanism and Fix](#f-p9-17-mechanism-and-fix-pull-request-16-2026-11-27)). This question, the release that carries the fix, stayed open until the owner decision above.

## F-P9-17 Mechanism and Fix (Pull Request 16) (2026-11-27)

The owner gave the go on 2026-11-27, in these words: "Go ahead and implement the Windows fix." That is the go for the fix in the repository. It is not a decision on the release that carries it: [the owner question](#owner-question-for-f-p9-17) (`0.2.1` or `0.3.0`) stays open. The package version, the release notes of a published version, and the ledger do not change. Pull request 16, on the branch `fix/f-p9-17-windows-wrapper-exit-code` from `main` at `8d81488`.

### The Tests First

`toolkits/buildos/test/wrapper-exit-codes.test.ts` (new) runs the project wrappers of this tree with the real `node` (on Windows the `node.exe` of the runner, no `node.cmd` stub) and a fake BuildOS program, which writes one line to stdout and one to stderr and exits with the code that the test gives it: `0`, `1`, `2`, `7`, and `127`. The program is reached through three routes that work offline: a local install (`node_modules/build-os` in the project), a global install (on Windows an npm `.cmd` shim on `PATH` with `node_modules\build-os` next to it, which the helper uses without running the shim), and `npx` (on Windows a copy of npm's own `npx.cmd` from the runner's Node.js folder, whose `npx-cli.js` is the fake). On Windows each `.cmd` wrapper starts three ways: `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<wrapper> args"` (as Node.js, CI runners, and agents start a `.cmd` file), `cmd.exe /d /s /c "call <wrapper> args"`, and from PowerShell (`pwsh`) as `& <wrapper> args` with `$LASTEXITCODE`. A driver batch file runs, under one `cmd.exe`, the helper as `buildos.cmd` starts it (`node.exe pinned-version.cjs --cmd <buildos.cmd> <manifest> some-command --flag`, with the two variables that `buildos.cmd` sets), then `call` of the wrapper, then a nested `cmd /d /s /c` of the wrapper, and reads `%ERRORLEVEL%` on the line right after each: the measurement that [F-P9-17 After Run 3](#f-p9-17-after-run-3-cause-narrowed) names as missing. Seven probe batch files show the `cmd.exe` rule apart from BuildOS. On macOS and Linux the `sh` wrappers get the same exit-code cases with the real `node` (directly and through `sh -c`; they passed before the fix too), and the Windows-only cases skip.

The first commit of the pull request (`d702c32`) has these tests and no wrapper change. Its `buildos-ci` run, [46066863403](https://github.com/brucewaynedecoy/build-os/actions/runs/46066863403), failed on `windows-latest` only, with 19 failing tests, all of them new (2,531 tests: 2,383 passed, 19 failed, 129 skipped); Linux and macOS passed. Each failing case stops at its first wrong code, so the logs show the program's `1` (or `2` for the `npx` legacy cases) and the wrapper's `0`, with the program's stderr line printed:

| Case (Windows, wrappers of `0.2.0`, run 46066863403) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `buildos.cmd`, `cmd /c`, local-install, global-install, and `npx` routes | exit `0` for program code `1` (failed) |
| `buildos.cmd`, PowerShell `&`, the three routes | `$LASTEXITCODE` `0` for program code `1` (failed) |
| `buildos.cmd`, `cmd /c call`, the three routes | each code kept: `0`, `1`, `2`, `7`, `127` (passed) |
| `buildos-intake.cmd`, `buildos-discovery.cmd`, `buildos-design.cmd`, `cmd /c` and PowerShell `&`, local-install route | exit `0` for program code `1` (failed) |
| The same three, `cmd /c call`, local-install route | each code kept (passed) |
| The same three, `cmd /c`, `npx` route with npm's own `npx.cmd` | exit `0` for program code `2` (failed) |
| `buildos.cmd`, `cmd /c`, a caller variable `ERRORLEVEL=0` | exit `0` for program code `2` (failed) |
| One `cmd.exe`, the three routes, program code `1` | `direct=1`, `call=1`, `nested=0` (failed on `nested`) |

The probes, each with a program that exits `2`; the three numbers are the exit code of `cmd.exe` for `cmd /c <file>`, for `cmd /c call <file>`, and for `cmd /c <file>` with a caller variable `ERRORLEVEL=0`:

| Probe batch file | Codes |
| --- | --- |
| The program, then `exit /b` | `0`, `2`, `0` |
| The program at the end of the file (the shape of npm's `npx.cmd`) | `2`, `2`, `2` |
| The program, then `goto :eof` | `0`, `2`, `0` |
| The program, then `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` | `2`, `2`, `0` |
| `setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion`, the program, then `exit /b` (the shape of `buildos.cmd` in `0.1.0` and `0.2.0`) | `0`, `2`, `0` |
| `setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion`, the program, then `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` | `2`, `2`, `0` |
| `setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion`, `set "ERRORLEVEL="`, the program, then `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` (the shape of the fix) | `2`, `2`, `2` |

### The Mechanism, as the Run Shows It

When `cmd /c` runs a `.cmd` file with no `call`, the exit code of `cmd.exe` is the code of the last command that ran in the file, not the `ERRORLEVEL`. A bare `exit /b` (or `goto :eof`) is such a command, with code `0`. So `buildos.cmd`, whose last line after `node` is a bare `exit /b`, gives `0` to every caller that starts it that way: `cmd /c`, and PowerShell, which starts a `.cmd` file through `cmd.exe /c`. With `call`, the code is the `ERRORLEVEL`, which `node` set, so the code is kept; npm's `npx.cmd` ends with the program itself, so it passes the code too. Microsoft's reference for `exit` says only that `exit /b <exitcode>` sets `ERRORLEVEL` and that `exit` outside a batch file sets the process exit code; it does not describe this case, so the rule is recorded as measured, not as documented. `pinned-version.cjs` is not involved: started directly, and under one `cmd.exe`, it returned the program's code on all three routes, also through npm's `npx.cmd`. The legacy `.cmd` scripts start `buildos.cmd` with no `call`, so `buildos.cmd` ends them, and they give what `buildos.cmd` gives. A variable named `ERRORLEVEL` in the caller's environment hides the real one in `%ERRORLEVEL%`, so `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` alone gives that variable's value.

### The Fix

`system/.os/scripts/buildos.cmd`, two lines and their comments. The last line of the normal path, after `node "%~dp0pinned-version.cjs" --cmd "%~f0" "%~dp0..\manifest.json" %*`, is now `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%` in place of `exit /b`; and right after `setlocal DisableDelayedExpansion` the wrapper runs `set "ERRORLEVEL="`, which removes a variable of that name from its own copy of the environment only. `%ERRORLEVEL%` is read on its own line after `node` has ended, so delayed expansion stays off. Every other line is the same: the arguments go on as `%*` with no `call`, so they are never read twice; `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath`, the loop guard, the Node.js check, and the start of the program by Node.js itself (no path comes back as text) do not change; the first lines that the helper reads to know a wrapper do not change. The legacy `.cmd` scripts and `pinned-version.cjs` do not change. `system/.os/scripts/AGENTS.md` now says that `buildos.cmd` ends with `exit /b %ERRORLEVEL%`, so the caller gets the exit code also without `call`, and why the wrapper removes an `ERRORLEVEL` variable. The probe test now asserts the codes above, and `test/rollback-smoke.test.ts` checks the new last line.

The wrapper files ship in the package (`dist/system/`, built from `system/`) and `buildos init` copies them byte for byte; no golden, managed-file hash, manifest contract, or parity exception pins their bytes, so no golden changed and no capture ran. An existing project does not get the fixed wrapper by itself: `buildos init` in a project that BuildOS already set up writes no wrapper (a rerun only refreshes its sections in the shared files), and the guide's upgrade steps from `0.1.0` to `0.2.0` change the version and four skills only. So an adopter on Windows gets the fix only by copying `.os/scripts/buildos.cmd` from the release that has it; the notes and the upgrade steps of that release must say so.

### The Guide

Chapter 4 says which versions have the defect, in place of "A fix is planned.": "On Windows, in BuildOS `0.1.0` and `0.2.0`, the project wrapper `.os\scripts\buildos.cmd` and the `.cmd` scripts with the old names give exit code `0` when they are started without `call`, for example by `cmd /c`, by PowerShell, or by an agent. The error text is right, so check the text, not only the code. The fix is in the BuildOS repository and waits for a release." The repeated claim says "or `0` on Windows through the project wrapper of `0.1.0` or `0.2.0`, as above". `guide/BuildOS-Guide.html` is rebuilt (`node tools/build-guide.mjs`).

### The Smokes

The rollback smoke runs only the published `0.1.0` and `0.2.0`, whose wrappers keep the defect, so its Windows checks of exit `0` (F-P9-17) stay true, and it has no mode that uses this tree's wrappers; it is not changed. The tarball and local-pack modes of `scripts/published-smoke.ts` use this tree's wrappers, but their wrapper steps check a command that succeeds and the Node.js-missing message (exit `127`), not a failing command; adding a failing-command wrapper step there is a follow-up for the release that carries the fix.

### What Stays Unproven

- npm's real `npx` with the registry: the tests use a copy of npm's own `npx.cmd` with a fake `npx-cli.js`, offline. The fixed wrapper on the real `npx` route with the registry runs only when a release with the fix is smoked.
- A real global install made by `npm install -g` on Windows: the test lays out the same files (an npm shim and the package next to it).
- An interactive Command Prompt (a person who types the wrapper, then `echo %ERRORLEVEL%`): not measured; the driver measures a batch file.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`): only `pwsh` ran.
- Exit codes outside `0` to `127`, and codes from a real BuildOS failure other than a usage error: the fake program covers the five codes above.

### The Run of the Fix

The `buildos-ci` run of the fix commit (`de7e8b6`), [46068381377](https://github.com/brucewaynedecoy/build-os/actions/runs/46068381377), passed on all jobs. On `windows-latest` the unit tests had 2,531 tests: 2,402 passed, 0 failed, 129 skipped; the golden harness had 299 tests: 294 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. The existing Windows wrapper tests of `test/wrappers.test.ts` (arguments with `%`, `^`, double quotes, `&`, and `!`, the loop guard, the Node.js messages, and the `PATH` rules) passed with the fixed wrapper. The new cases, on Windows:

| Wrapper | Route | `cmd /c` | `cmd /c call` | PowerShell `&` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buildos.cmd` | local install, global install, `npx` (npm's own `npx.cmd`) | `0`, `1`, `2`, `7`, `127` kept (passed) | kept (passed) | kept (passed) |
| `buildos-intake.cmd`, `buildos-discovery.cmd`, `buildos-design.cmd` | local install | kept (passed) | kept (passed) | kept (passed) |
| The same three | `npx` (npm's own `npx.cmd`) | `2` kept (passed) | not run | not run |
| `buildos.cmd`, a caller variable `ERRORLEVEL=0` | local install | `2` kept (passed) | not run | not run |

Under one `cmd.exe`, on the three routes, `%ERRORLEVEL%` was the program's code after the helper started directly, after `call` of the wrapper, and after a nested `cmd /c` of the wrapper, for each of the five codes. The seven probes gave the same codes as in the first run, now asserted. On Linux and macOS the `sh` cases passed.

## Release Route for 0.2.1 (2026-11-27)

### Owner Decision of 2026-11-27 (0.2.1 Release Route)

The orchestrator asked the owner on 2026-11-27: "How do we release 0.2.1? 1. Short checklist now, rebuild after. You get 7 steps. The agents do all checks before your first step. The full workflow rebuild comes after 0.2.1. 2. Rebuild first." The owner answered, word for word: "Option 1." The owner was told that option 1 changes three things from the [Release Runbook for 0.2.0](#release-runbook-for-020): (a) the owner's "accept" reply in owner step 1 counts as the release approval, with no second written approval later; (b) two checks move to after the release: the signing-log (Rekor) check of the staged file and the speed measurement (`PERF-002`); (c) the record goes into the next pull request, with no separate record pull request after the release. No other owner decision is recorded here.

### Release Checklist for 0.2.1

The short route of the decision above. Where a command is the same as in the [Release Runbook for 0.2.0](#release-runbook-for-020), the step names the runbook step, with `0.2.1` for the new version and `0.2.0` for the previous one. `<H1>` is the full SHA of the reviewed head of this pull request, `<H2>` the ledger commit on top of it, `<run>` and `<attempt>` the run ID and attempt of the `<H1>` dry run, `<sha256>` its tarball SHA-256, and `$D` a new empty folder outside the repository (`D=$(mktemp -d)`).

Agent steps, before the owner's first step. Each passes, with its run ID in the evidence, or the release stops.

1. The dry run of `<H1>` (orchestrator). The branch is up to date with `main`, and nothing else merges into `main` until the tag. From the repository root: `git push origin <H1>:refs/heads/release-dry-run/0.2.1`. A push to a `release-dry-run/` branch is a dry run with candidates `self`. Every gate passes (runbook step b).
2. Inspect the tarball (every check of runbook step c): the SHA-256 equals `tarball_sha256` in `release-build.json`; the file list; `npm diff --diff=build-os@0.2.0 --diff="$D/artifact/build-os-0.2.1.tgz"`; the offline install; `version --json` reports `0.2.1` and `<H1>`; the SBOM; the real-list deny-list scan of the tarball (0 matches); the size and file count against `0.2.0`.
3. The smoke on three systems on that tarball (runbook step c): `gh workflow run buildos-smoke.yml --repo brucewaynedecoy/build-os --ref main -f source=release-run -f release_run=<run> -f release_run_attempt=<attempt> -f tarball_sha256=<sha256>`; each report has `tarball.version` `0.2.1`.
4. The upgrade and the rollback with that tarball, in `sh` on macOS or Linux: the guide's "From 0.2.0 to 0.2.1" and "Roll back from 0.2.1 to 0.2.0", in a project made by `npx -y build-os@0.2.0 init --skip-make-docs`, with the guide's offline form of step 2 on that file and an install of that file as the `0.2.1` install. The record says what did not run: the Command Prompt and PowerShell forms, without a Windows machine.
5. The ledger entry, as a second commit `<H2>` on this pull request's branch. In `toolkits/buildos/` of a clean checkout of `<H1>`: `node scripts/release-candidate.ts compute --tarball "$D/artifact/build-os-0.2.1.tgz" --build "$D/artifact/release-build.json" --reviewed-by brucewaynedecoy --reviewed-on <YYYY-MM-DD> --evidence "<text>"`. The build record names `<H1>`, so the entry's `source_commit` is `<H1>`. Add the printed entry after the `v0.2.0` entry. `node scripts/release-candidate.ts check` and `node scripts/release-candidate.ts verify --tag v0.2.1 --tarball "$D/artifact/build-os-0.2.1.tgz"` pass, and `git diff --name-only <H1> <H2>` prints only `toolkits/buildos/release-candidates.json` (commit type `chore`, no history record, as in runbook step d). Then the dry run of `<H2>` with candidates `committed`. A push to a `release-dry-run/` branch always uses `self`, so it is a hand-started run on this pull request's branch, while its head is `<H2>`: `gh workflow run buildos-release.yml --repo brucewaynedecoy/build-os --ref release/0.2.1-version -f purpose=dry-run -f tag=v0.2.1 -f candidates=committed -f plant=none`. Its summary names commit `<H2>` and candidates `committed`, and every gate passes: the identity gate accepts `<H1>`, because `<H1>` is an ancestor of `<H2>` and the two differ only in the ledger (`sourceCommitProblems` in `scripts/release-gate.ts`), and the digest gate rebuilds with the source revision `<H1>` and gets `<sha256>` again. The same holds at the tag only for a merge commit: a squash merge makes a commit that does not have `<H1>` as an ancestor, and the gate stops.
6. An independent review of `<H2>` (the ledger change only).

Owner steps.

1. Read the orchestrator's one-page summary. Reply "accept 0.2.1" with the SHA-256 `<sha256>`. This reply is the recorded publication approval.
2. Merge this pull request with "Create a merge commit". Never squash.
3. Tag and draft. From the repository root:

   ```sh
   git fetch origin
   git diff --name-only <H1> origin/main
   git tag v0.2.1 origin/main
   git push origin refs/tags/v0.2.1
   D=$(mktemp -d)
   git show v0.2.1:toolkits/buildos/RELEASE_NOTES.md | awk '/^## 0\.2\.1$/{p=1;next} /^## /{p=0} p' | grep -v '^Status: draft' > "$D/notes-0.2.1.md"
   grep '^##' "$D/notes-0.2.1.md"
   gh release create v0.2.1 --repo brucewaynedecoy/build-os --draft --verify-tag --title "BuildOS 0.2.1" --notes-file "$D/notes-0.2.1.md"
   ```

   The `git diff` prints only `toolkits/buildos/release-candidates.json`; if it prints more, stop. The tag push prints the "Bypassed rule violations" notice of the `release tags` ruleset, as for `0.2.0`. The `grep` prints exactly five headings, in this order: `### Fixed`, `### Update a project from 0.2.0`, `### Known limits`, `### Check the package`, `### Roll back`.

4. Start the prepare run: `gh workflow run buildos-release.yml --repo brucewaynedecoy/build-os --ref main -f purpose=prepare -f tag=v0.2.1 -f candidates=committed -f plant=none`.
5. When the orchestrator says "ready" (the agent checked the prepare run, the two draft assets, their digest, release immutability, and the rulesets through the API, as in runbook step f): publish the draft, `gh release edit v0.2.1 --repo brucewaynedecoy/build-os --draft=false`. The release run starts. When it waits at `Stage on npm (approval with 2FA needed)`, approve the `buildos-npm-stage` deployment on the run page (Review deployments > Approve and deploy).
6. Approve the stage on npm: `npm stage list build-os` lists the stage ID that the orchestrator read from the stage job's log; then `npm stage approve <stage-id>` (2FA).
7. `npm view build-os versions dist-tags --json`: `versions` holds `0.2.1`, and `latest` is `0.2.1`. If `latest` is not `0.2.1`, run `npm dist-tag add build-os@0.2.1 latest` (2FA).

After publication (agents; the results go into the next pull request): the registry digest equals the ledger (`npm pack build-os@0.2.1` and its SHA-256); `npm audit signatures` in a new folder; the Rekor lookup of runbook h1, on the registry tarball; the registry smoke on three systems (`-f source=registry -f version=0.2.1`); `PERF-002`, in the order of runbook step k; then the documentation pull request: remove the draft status line of the `0.2.1` notes, move the smoke default to `0.2.1` with its test, and check each row of [Facts That Depend on the 0.2.1 Release](#facts-that-depend-on-the-021-release).

### Departures From the Written Rules (Owner Exception for 0.2.1)

These departures are the dated owner exception of 2026-11-27 ("Option 1."), for `0.2.1` only. This pull request does not change the written rules: the workflow rebuild after `0.2.1` changes them in its own pull request.

| Written rule | For 0.2.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `SECURITY.md`, Release Procedure step 6 and Maintainer Checklist; `toolkits/buildos/AGENTS.md`, Release and First Publication step 6; A81 and runbook steps i and j: the stage is approved on npm only after the recorded publication approval, which comes after the checks of the stage and names the stage ID | The recorded approval is the owner's "accept 0.2.1" reply of owner step 1, before staging. It names the tarball SHA-256, not a stage ID, because no stage exists yet. No second written approval follows. The stage is bound to that SHA-256 by the workflow: the `stage` job stages only the release asset whose SHA-256 equals the ledger entry, after the release run's fresh rebuild gave the same SHA-256 (Release Procedure, "What this guarantees"). The agent records the reply in the next pull request |
| `SECURITY.md`, Maintainer Checklist: after staging, check the staged package's provenance and digest; runbook h1 | After publication: the Rekor lookup runs on the registry tarball, as it did for `0.2.0` |
| Runbook h4: the performance check before the approval | `PERF-002` runs after publication, as for `0.2.0`: its instrument measures only a published package |
| Runbook step k: the publication record, then a documentation pull request | The record goes into the next pull request, with no separate record pull request |
| `toolkits/buildos/AGENTS.md`, Release, and the header of `scripts/release-candidate.ts`: the dry run on `release-dry-run/<short-sha>`; the ledger entry in its own pull request with nothing else | The dry-run branch is `release-dry-run/0.2.1`; the workflow takes any `release-dry-run/**` branch, and a name with `-plant-` would plant a failure. The ledger entry is the second commit `<H2>` of this pull request. The identity gate checks commits, not pull requests: `<H1>` is an ancestor of the tag commit and differs from it only in the ledger |
| Runbook step d: the owner accepts the tarball before the entry is computed | The entry, with `--reviewed-by brucewaynedecoy`, is computed before owner step 1. The owner's reply accepts the tarball with that SHA-256; without it, the pull request is not merged |
